source.title: Freeze and Chaos for DNNs: an NTK view of Batch Normalization, Checkerboard and Boundary Effects
source.authors: Arthur Jacot; Franck Gabriel; Clément Hongler

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices; some references and a few formula characters are garbled, but the relevant sections are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes training behavior through infinite-width NTK theory and numerical GAN experiments, but it does not measure training classification error on the listed benchmarks or directly test most version recipes.
record.gate_note: Own results concern NTK behavior and GAN mode collapse, including theoretical statements that order slows training and chaos ensures fast training. These bear on the broad training claim and BN's optimization role but do not report CIFAR training classification error, local-minimum frequencies, or classification-training outcomes for the specified depth, initialization, or learning-rate recipes. Figure 4.1 and Figure A.1 include GAN samples, but the text gives no numerical sample-quality or mode-collapse metric. Reference-only claims about cited prior work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study reports NTK geometry and qualitative GAN outcomes, not the training error, training speed, trainable depth, local-minimum frequency or learning-rate stability outcomes named by V1–V6. Its BN result controls a kernel component; it does not establish faster accuracy gains or greater learning-rate tolerance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that ordered NTKs favor constant modes and checkerboard patterns, slowing training and potentially contributing to GAN mode collapse. They propose nonlinearity normalization, parent-based parametrization and layer-dependent learning rates, supported by theoretical analysis and qualitative numerical illustrations.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies infinite-width NTK kernels and qualitative GAN behavior, not benchmark classification error or the specified BN accuracy-speed comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Theoretical behavior depends on the order/chaos regime, indexed by the nonlinearity and bias parameter; GAN behavior is shown under different nonlinearity/normalization choices. The paper reports qualitative differences among ReLU, normalized ReLU, and ReLU with Batch Normalization in Figure 4.1.

fits_no_version.finding: In infinite-width fully connected networks, increasing depth makes the normalized NTK approach a constant in order and a Kronecker delta in chaos. The authors interpret these limits as slowing training and impairing generalization, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation and bias choices determine depth-dependent NTK geometry and its implications for optimization.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-nonlinearity BN after the last hidden layer controls the constant component of the NTK Gram matrix.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A final hidden-layer BN operation suppresses the constant NTK component associated with the ordered regime.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report checkerboard mode collapse for ordered ReLU generators and qualitative successful generation with normalized ReLU without BN; they also display BN samples. Parent-based parametrization and layer-dependent learning rates address spatial artifacts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization, parametrization and layer-dependent learning rates affect checkerboard artifacts and mode collapse in DCGAN generators.

record.problems: The classification and training-speed outcomes named by the claim versions are not measured. The GAN evidence is qualitative, with no numerical sample-quality, collapse-rate, accuracy, or training-speed metric. Much of the analysis is an infinite-width limit and may not directly quantify finite-network training.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results were left out. Figure 4.1 and Figure A.1 provide qualitative image displays without a text-described metric; R4 records the BN image condition, while the other figure conditions are covered by the text-described qualitative outcomes in R2 and R3.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels, and its dependence on size, optimization and regularization.
Spurious local-minimum frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training error in matched plain and residual networks, longer-training controls, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Initialization comparisons measuring learning speed or trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and very deep plain convolutional networks.
Loss, curvature and divergence trajectories relative to learning-rate stability thresholds. Layer-dependent learning rates here address layer contributions and artifacts instead.
Matched BN versus non-BN accuracy trajectories and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's comparative training speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdict is warranted. The absence of the named outcome measures is an untested component, not evidence against the claims. The qualitative findings remain valid related results.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 classification error, corrupted or random labels, model size, optimizer, regularization, and early stopping.
Teacher-student ReLU training, spurious minima frequencies, and student width comparisons.
Plain versus residual classification networks, their training errors and training duration, plus Fixup and very deep plain-network outcomes.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, trainable depth and speed comparisons, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional classification training.
Learning-rate stability threshold experiments, loss trajectories, curvature/sharpness, and divergence comparisons.

Does not measure accuracy gain over training steps or compare learning-rate tolerance of matched BN and non-BN classifiers. Its BN analysis uses post-nonlinearity BN in the theoretical FC-NN setting; its GAN illustration does not quantify comparative training speed.

rows.subject: FC-NN with a PN-BN after the last nonlinearity
rows.size_stated: infinite-width limit; widths sequentially tend to infinity
rows.stage_stated: training dynamics analyzed in the infinite-width limit
rows.operation_detail: Proves that the constant Rayleigh quotient of the NTK Gram matrix is controlled by a post-last-nonlinearity batch-normalization layer.
rows.measure: Constant Rayleigh quotient of the NTK Gram matrix, (1/N)1ᵀΘ̃(L)1
rows.note: This is an NTK geometry result, not an accuracy or training-speed measure, so it cannot establish the version's faster accuracy gains.
rows.check: The Rayleigh quotient measures NTK geometry, not V6's training-speed or learning-rate effect. Add the stated theoretical comparator: approximately cN in extreme order, versus the reported β² with post-nonlinearity BN. The centering argument in Appendix D does not require infinite width.

rows.subject: DCGAN generator on CelebA with graph-based parametrization and layer-dependent learning rate
rows.operation_detail: Trains with ReLU nonlinearity and no batch normalization; reports generator collapse to a checkerboard mode in the ordered regime.
rows.value: The ordered regime leads to a collapse of the generator to a checkerboard mode.
rows.note: The paper states the behavior, but no numerical rate or matched BN training-speed comparison is given.
rows.check: Qualitative generator collapse is reported, but it does not measure any version's outcome. In particular, collapse without BN does not establish BN's effect on accuracy gain or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: DCGAN generator on CelebA with graph-based parametrization and layer-dependent learning rate
rows.operation_detail: Tunes nonlinearity and parametrization to reach the chaotic regime and trains without batch normalization.
rows.measure: GAN sample quality / avoidance of checkerboard mode
rows.value: The authors state they obtain good quality samples and avoid the checkerboard mode; no numerical measure is stated.
rows.note: The paper's qualitative GAN outcome is not a training-speed or classification-accuracy comparison.
rows.check: Qualitative sample quality and avoidance of collapse under normalized ReLU do not measure V6. Successful GAN training without BN also does not test the specific Fixup claim.

rows.subject: DCGAN generator on CelebA with graph-based parametrization and layer-dependent learning rate
rows.operation_detail: Trains with batch normalization; Figure 4.1 depicts the generated samples.
rows.note: Figure displays generated images, with no text-described quantitative outcome or comparative speed.
rows.check: Generated-image displays provide no comparative training-speed or learning-rate result. Keep this as a qualitative illustration rather than evidence for V6.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
